options.B: A weak opioid such as tramadol
options.C: Intravenous morphine immediately
options.D: A high-dose steroid alone

explanation: Step 2 of the WHO pain ladder introduces weak opioids when non-opioids are no longer enough to control pain. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h5)

question: What tissue type largely replaces active muscle fibers in the frequently pregnant uterus?

options.A: Adipose fatty tissue
options.B: Epithelial lining tissue
options.C: Smooth cartilage tissue
options.D: Fibrous connective tissue

explanation: Repeated stretching causes the myometrium to accumulate fibrous tissue, diminishing overall contractile efficiency. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h2)

question: What does psychological safety mean in a healthcare team?

options.A: Ensuring nurses never experience physical fatigue on duty
options.B: Feeling safe to speak up without fear of retaliation
options.C: Having physical security guards stationed in every ward
options.D: Guaranteed job security for all tenured staff members

explanation: Psychological safety enables workers to voice concerns, report errors, and suggest improvements without fear of negative consequences. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h3)

question: How does an essential drug list improve safety for clinical staff?

options.A: By replacing traditional nursing documentation with automated software
options.B: By limiting the number of drugs workers must master, reducing prescribing errors
options.C: By completely eliminating the need for nurses to administer injections
options.D: By shifting all diagnostic responsibilities away from primary care clinics

explanation: Familiarity with a focused group of medicines helps clinicians know dosages, contraindications, and side effects thoroughly. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: The main objective of a community health risk assessment is to achieve what outcome?

options.A: Increase in pharmaceutical manufacturing plants in rural zones
options.B: Reduction of hospital bed capacities in urban centers
options.C: Disease prevention and health promotion tailored to local needs
options.D: Elimination of traditional medicine practices across the country

explanation: Assessments aim directly at preventing illness and promoting wellness based on local findings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is a common complication of severely underfeeding a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and muscle wasting
options.B: Rapid accumulation of excess adipose tissue
options.C: Acute fatty liver disease and high blood sugar
options.D: Dangerous fluid overload in the lung cavities

explanation: Insufficient energy and nutrient intake deprives the body of resources needed to repair tissues and maintain muscle mass. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h8)

question: A nurse manager panics and changes shift policies because patient wait times increased slightly due to normal seasonal illnesses. What mistake was made?

options.A: Failing to apply ethical knowing to administrative scheduling
options.B: Ignoring special cause variation during an active outbreak
options.C: Treating common cause variation as special cause variation
options.D: Relying entirely on aesthetic knowing for workflow design

explanation: Reacting to normal, expected fluctuations as if they stem from an unusual event leads to chaotic and counterproductive management decisions. [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the term for when the body takes absorbed nutrients and builds them into body tissues?

options.A: Peristalsis
options.B: Excretion
options.C: Ingestion
options.D: Assimilation

explanation: Assimilation is how the body uses absorbed nutrients to build and repair cell structures. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h1)

question: Why is prompt reporting of new joint swelling after PROM important?

options.A: It means the patient is ready for full independent discharge
options.B: It signals that the room temperature is too high
options.C: It proves the exercises successfully increased muscle mass
options.D: It could indicate acute tissue injury or micro-trauma

explanation: Unexplained swelling or redness after movement can signify a tear, strain, or other injury requiring medical review. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)

question: When does an endemic disease turn into an epidemic?

options.A: The geographic spread shrinks to a single village
options.B: The infection rate drops to zero for several consecutive months
options.C: Scientists change the classification name every ten years
options.D: Case numbers suddenly exceed the normal expected baseline

explanation: An epidemic occurs when the incidence rate rises significantly higher than what is normally expected for that population. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h2)

question: Which body tissue burns the most energy at rest, helping to raise a person's metabolic rate?

options.A: Fibrous tissue
options.B: Adipose tissue
options.C: Bone matrix
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Muscle tissue is very active and needs a steady supply of nutrients and oxygen even at rest, unlike fat tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h2)

question: What common symptom do some patients report during the early stages of elevated blood pressure?

options.A: Complete loss of peripheral vision
options.B: Severe pain in the lower legs
options.C: Morning occipital headaches
options.D: Sudden swelling of both ankles

explanation: Early morning headaches located at the back of the head are a classic, though inconsistent, warning sign. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h5)

question: What would happen if the endothelial lining (tunica intima) of a blood vessel becomes damaged?

options.A: The tunica media dissolves due to exposure to plasma
options.B: Blood pressure in that specific vessel drops immediately to zero
options.C: Oxygen exchange in nearby capillaries stops permanently
options.D: Platelets may stick to the rough surface and form a clot

explanation: A smooth endothelium prevents inappropriate coagulation; damage exposes underlying collagen, triggering platelet adhesion and thrombus formation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of a parasite in medical science?

options.A: A beneficial microbe that aids in human digestion
options.B: An organism living on a host and benefiting at its expense
options.C: Any living creature found inside the human intestinal tract
options.D: A microscopic organism that always kills its host immediately

explanation: Parasites survive by taking vital nutrients from a host organism while offering no physiological advantage back. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why is immediate linkage to care important during post-test counselling for a positive result?

options.A: It proves that the laboratory equipment is functioning properly
options.B: It prevents the client from ever talking about their diagnosis
options.C: It ensures timely initiation of treatment and viral suppression
options.D: It removes the need for any future emotional support

explanation: Connecting diagnosed individuals to ART quickly improves long-term health outcomes and reduces community transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h3)

question: How can family members best support a visually impaired relative without hindering recovery?

options.A: Limiting social visitors to protect them from emotional stress
options.B: Insisting the patient stay indoors to avoid potential public accidents
options.C: Encouraging independence while offering help only when requested
options.D: Taking over all daily self-care tasks to eliminate any mistakes

explanation: Balanced support fosters self-reliance and prevents the negative psychological effects of overprotection. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h7)

question: What is the primary type of data collected in quantitative research?

options.A: Narrative stories
options.B: Visual paintings
options.C: Audio recordings
options.D: Numerical data

explanation: Quantitative research focuses on gathering numbers and measurable quantities to analyze trends and test hypotheses. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is physical assessment of a patient more difficult inside a moving ambulance?

options.A: Engine noise and vehicle vibration obscure findings
options.B: Lighting inside ambulances is always completely dark
options.C: Medical equipment automatically shuts down in motion
options.D: Nurses are legally forbidden to touch patients

explanation: Vibrations and sounds make auscultation with a stethoscope and visual inspection challenging during active transit. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which enzyme found in saliva initiates the breakdown of complex carbohydrates?

options.A: Salivary amylase
options.B: Pepsinogen
options.C: Pancreatic lipase
options.D: Carboxypeptidase

explanation: Salivary amylase targets starches in the mouth, splitting them into smaller sugars like maltose. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why are trans fats considered more harmful to heart health than other unsaturated fats?

options.A: They block the liver from metabolizing basic dietary carbohydrates.
options.B: They increase low-density lipoprotein cholesterol while reducing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
options.C: They prevent the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins in the small intestine.
options.D: They store excessive amounts of water within the subcutaneous adipose tissue.

explanation: Industrial trans fats negatively alter blood cholesterol by raising bad LDL cholesterol and lowering good HDL cholesterol at the same time. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism infusion pumps use to deliver fluids?

options.A: Atmospheric suction
options.B: Capillary action
options.C: Gravitational pull
options.D: Positive pressure

explanation: Infusion pumps actively push fluids through the administration set using positive pressure rather than relying strictly on gravity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary reason for zoning an RRC into clean and contaminated areas?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and protect uninfected individuals
options.B: To make the physical building look more professional and tidy
options.C: To organize administrative paperwork and patient filing systems
options.D: To separate male patients from female patients during admission

explanation: Physical separation of zones stops pathogens from spreading from infectious patients to clean zones or staff rest areas. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why is kitchen hygiene important during meal preparation?

options.A: To meet export standards
options.B: To speed up crop harvesting
options.C: To raise the market value of leftovers
options.D: To prevent germs and foodborne illnesses

explanation: Clean preparation spaces and utensils stop harmful bacteria and parasites from spreading through family meals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h6)

question: Why is community health advocacy an important nursing duty?

options.A: It replaces the need for doctors in rural clinics
options.B: It guarantees that hospitals receive adequate funding
options.C: It addresses environmental and social factors affecting lung health
options.D: It eliminates all infectious diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses advocate for changes in policies and habits that tackle the root environmental causes of illness. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h7)

question: Why is the use of standardized nursing terminologies essential in electronic health records?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing hospital computer hardware
options.B: It completely removes the need for nurses to write narrative nursing notes
options.C: It ensures clear communication and allows evaluation of nursing care outcomes
options.D: It stops patients from viewing their own electronic medical charts

explanation: Standardized languages create a uniform way to track interventions and outcomes, improving continuity and research quality. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary role of a nurse manager in financial control?

options.A: Writing the national health budget
options.B: Setting tax rates for medical services
options.C: Auditing external hospital accounts
options.D: Acting as a frontline financial steward

explanation: Nurse managers directly oversee unit resources, making them frontline stewards of institutional funds. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h1)

question: What happens to toxoid and adjuvanted vaccines if they are accidentally frozen in the cold chain?

options.A: They require dilution with warm sterile water before use
options.B: Their expiration date extends by an extra six months
options.C: Their potency is permanently destroyed and they become unsafe
options.D: They convert automatically into live-attenuated viral strains

explanation: Freezing alters the aluminum adjuvant structure in toxoid and killed vaccines, ruining their ability to stimulate immunity. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why is monitoring patient outcomes necessary after introducing a researched change?

options.A: To confirm if the new practice truly improves clinical care
options.B: To prove to the hospital accountant that money was spent well
options.C: To satisfy legal requirements for nursing license renewal
options.D: To ensure the original authors get cited in future audits

explanation: Tracking outcomes ensures that the new evidence actually delivers the expected benefits in real-world practice. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary aim of studying the natural history of a disease?

options.A: To calculate the total financial profit of pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To design hospital building layouts for emergency wards
options.C: To find out when the specific disease was first discovered in history
options.D: To understand how the disease progresses without medical intervention

explanation: Natural history tracks disease progression from exposure through clinical manifestation to resolution or death. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h4)

question: A researcher notices room temperature is affecting patient recovery rates during a drug trial. What is room temperature classified as?

options.A: Independent variable
options.B: Dependent variable
options.C: Random variable
options.D: Extraneous variable

explanation: Any outside factor that influences the dependent variable without being part of the planned study is an extraneous variable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which pelvic type is considered the ideal, classic female pelvis for vaginal delivery?

options.A: Platypelloid
options.B: Android
options.C: Gynecoid
options.D: Anthropoid

explanation: The gynecoid pelvis has rounded contours and spacious dimensions that favor uncomplicated vaginal birth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the main function of pulmonary surfactant?

options.A: Trap dust particles and bacteria in the airway
options.B: Lower surface tension to prevent alveolar collapse
options.C: Maintain fluid balance inside the pleural cavity
options.D: Transport oxygen molecules through the blood plasma

explanation: Surfactant reduces the cohesive forces of water molecules inside the alveoli, stopping them from sticking together and collapsing. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do poor transportation networks negatively affect community problem identification?

options.A: They increase the accuracy of secondary hospital records
options.B: They force community members to visit teaching hospitals daily
options.C: They prevent nurses from reaching remote settlements to gather data
options.D: They automatically solve sanitation problems in urban slums

explanation: Bad roads and difficult terrain restrict physical access to hard-to-reach populations, leaving their health needs undocumented. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: What happens to ovulation after a client undergoes tubal ligation?

options.A: Ovaries stop producing female hormones
options.B: Eggs are trapped inside the uterine wall
options.C: Menstruation ceases completely forever
options.D: Ovaries continue releasing eggs normally

explanation: Tubal ligation blocks the tubes, not the ovaries, meaning hormonal production and ovulation continue as usual. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h2)

question: A nursing mother complains that her milk only flows after the baby sucks for a minute. What explains this?

options.A: Inhibition of progesterone by infant saliva
options.B: The milk ejection reflex triggered by oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin accumulation in the milk ducts
options.D: Alveolar breakdown releasing stored nutrients

explanation: Baby suckling triggers the release of oxytocin, which makes the muscles around the milk glands contract and push the milk down the ducts. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: Which organ is responsible for producing most plasma proteins?

options.A: Liver
options.B: Kidney
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Spleen

explanation: The liver synthesizes the vast majority of plasma proteins, including albumin, fibrinogen, and most transport globulins. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do community midwives manage nighttime deliveries in areas without electricity?

options.A: Performing all deliveries outside under moonlight
options.B: Using solar-powered lanterns and portable touchlights
options.C: Using open kerosene stoves for bright lighting
options.D: Waiting until sunrise before assisting the mother

explanation: Reliable alternative light sources like solar lanterns and touchlights are essential for maintaining visibility during nocturnal births in rural settings. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h4)

question: Where can completed paper ADR forms be submitted within Nigeria?

options.A: Commercial banks handling health insurance
options.B: Local police stations for criminal investigation
options.C: NAFDAC zonal offices or designated committees
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education headquarters

explanation: Completed reports are channeled through institutional drug committees or directly to NAFDAC zonal offices for processing. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h7)

question: A nurse notices that an instrument tray has a small tear in its paper wrapper just before a surgical procedure. What action should be taken?

options.A: Reject the tray and obtain a newly sterilized replacement pack.
options.B: Cover the tear with ordinary adhesive plaster and proceed.
options.C: Use the instruments immediately before ambient air contaminates them.
options.D: Spray the outside of the torn wrapper with a surface antiseptic.

explanation: A torn wrapper compromises the sterile barrier, meaning the contents are no longer considered sterile and must be reprocessed or replaced. [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h7)

question: What is the main goal of adding palliative care to cancer treatment?

options.A: Accelerating the terminal disease process to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Preventing family members from visiting the patient in the ward
options.C: Improving quality of life by managing pain and emotional distress
options.D: Replacing all standard chemotherapy protocols with herbal medicine

explanation: Palliative care focuses on whole-person comfort, helping manage physical symptoms and emotional stress for both the patient and their family. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is the primary effector of the somatic nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine glands
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle
options.D: Cardiac muscle

explanation: The somatic nervous system specifically targets and controls voluntary skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h5)

question: What does the relevance principle require when choosing essential medicines?

options.A: Selection based purely on international popularity
options.B: Preference for remedies requested by private marketers
options.C: Inclusion of every newly invented molecule on earth
options.D: Alignment with local disease patterns and health needs

explanation: Medicines are chosen because they directly target the actual illnesses affecting the local population. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of biochemical assessment over dietary histories in clinical practice?

options.A: It takes less time to perform
options.B: It costs significantly less money
options.C: It avoids subjective reporting errors
options.D: It relies on patient memory

explanation: Biochemical tests use objective laboratory measurements instead of depending on what a patient remembers or reports about their diet. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h1)

question: Unity of command ensures that an individual staff nurse reports to:

options.A: Multiple department heads simultaneously
options.B: Any senior doctor on duty
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: Only one designated direct supervisor

explanation: Unity of command dictates that an employee should receive orders from and report to only one supervisor to avoid conflicting instructions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a controlled vocabulary in a medical database?

options.A: To automatically translate research papers from English into local Nigerian languages
options.B: To restrict hospital internet access to approved medical websites only
options.C: To assign standardized terms to clinical concepts and overcome keyword variations
options.D: To calculate the statistical significance of clinical trial results

explanation: Controlled vocabularies unify different words used by various authors for the same medical condition under one official heading. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which clinical finding is most characteristic of fat embolism syndrome following a long bone fracture?

options.A: Sudden severe hypertension and bradycardia
options.B: Localized muscle spasms in the injured calf
options.C: Petechial rash over the chest and neck
options.D: Excessive local bleeding at the pin sites

explanation: A distinct petechial rash caused by small vessel occlusion from fat droplets is a classic late sign of fat embolism syndrome, alongside respiratory distress. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why is high crowd density dangerous even before a panic starts?

options.A: Loud noise causes permanent hearing damage
options.B: Heavy sweating leads to rapid dehydration and loss of body salts
options.C: Being near strangers causes severe stress and sudden heart attacks
options.D: Crowd crushing restricts chest movement and stops normal breathing

explanation: Extreme crowd density causes physical crushing forces that prevent normal chest wall movement, leading to compressive asphyxiation. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do patients taking D-penicillamine long-term need regular urine tests?

options.A: To measure the exact bacterial load in the bladder.
options.B: To check if the patient is eating enough dietary carbohydrates.
options.C: To confirm that the patient is drinking alkaline water.
options.D: To monitor for protein loss in the urine.

explanation: D-penicillamine can affect the filters in the kidneys, causing protein to leak into the urine as an early sign of toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h5)

question: How can a community health nurse best address local distrust during a health survey?

options.A: Conducting all interviews entirely in foreign languages
options.B: Ignoring local concerns and proceeding without consultation
options.C: Partnering with respected local leaders and traditional rulers
options.D: Relying solely on police escorts to enforce participation

explanation: Working through trusted community figures helps build rapport and reassures residents about the safety and purpose of the data collection. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which food group is an excellent natural source of both soluble and insoluble fiber for diabetic patients?

options.A: Refined vegetable oils
options.B: Processed white bread
options.C: Legumes and whole grains
options.D: Sweetened fruit juices

explanation: Beans, lentils, and whole grains are rich in fiber, making them ideal for blood sugar management and gut health. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h6)

question: What simple physical screening tool do nurses use to identify severe acute malnutrition in children during disasters?

options.A: A standard adult blood pressure cuff
options.B: A flexible vinyl waist measurement tape
options.C: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference tape
options.D: A rigid wooden height measurement board

explanation: MUAC tapes provide a fast, reliable physical measurement of muscle wasting and nutritional status in emergency field conditions. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h5)

question: A person's internal, deeply felt sense of being male or female is called what?

options.A: Biological sex
options.B: Social role
options.C: Gender expression
options.D: Gender identity

explanation: Gender identity describes the internal psychological awareness of one's own gender, distinct from external presentation or biology. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why must suspected Ebola patients be placed in immediate isolation upon arrival?

options.A: To prevent family members from bringing forbidden local foods
options.B: To comply with administrative rules without clinical benefit
options.C: To ensure they receive specialized high-cost surgical procedures
options.D: To prevent nosocomial transmission to other patients and staff

explanation: Immediate isolation halts the spread of the virus within the healthcare facility, protecting vulnerable patients and workers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h6)
